accepted.s: C.V. Raman received the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on
accepted.x: C.V. Raman was awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering and explaining the Raman Effect, involving the scattering of light.
accepted.tq: Direct field-of-contribution recall.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Har Gobind Khorana — Structure and function of the ribosome
S. Chandrasekhar — Experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
Venkatraman Ramakrishnan — Structure and function of the ribosome
Abhijit Banerjee — Interpreting the genetic code
accepted.x: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome.
accepted.tq: Match the scientist with the precise contribution; reject swapped achievements.
accepted.sec: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1968.
2. His Nobel-recognised work concerned interpretation of the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis.
3. He was a United States citizen when he received the Nobel Prize.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Khorana received the 1968 Medicine Nobel for work on the genetic code and was a US citizen at the time of the award.
accepted.tq: Verify the year, field and citizenship together rather than relying on nationality alone.
accepted.sec: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Abhijit Banerjee shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for
o: the mathematical theory of black holes
an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
the discovery of the Raman Effect
research on the structure of the ribosome
accepted.x: Abhijit Banerjee, along with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer, received the 2019 Economics Nobel for an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the award-winning contribution.
accepted.sec: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the contribution recognised by the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to S. Chandrasekhar?
o: Physical processes in the structure and evolution of stars
accepted.x: S. Chandrasekhar received the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for theoretical studies of the physical processes governing the structure and evolution of stars, particularly white dwarfs.
accepted.tq: Use the exact contribution, avoiding the look-alike claim about black-hole theory.
accepted.sec: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913?
accepted.x: Rabindranath Tagore received the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature and was the first Indian and Asian Nobel laureate.
accepted.tq: Link the award year to the laureate; distinguish literature from science awards.
accepted.sec: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ronald Ross is associated with the discovery that malaria is caused by the
accepted.x: Ronald Ross received the 1902 Nobel Prize in Medicine for establishing the role of the Plasmodium parasite in malaria.
accepted.tq: Direct association of scientist, discovery and disease.
accepted.sec: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship - field, year, discovery; FIRST scientist laureate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes C.V. Raman from S. Chandrasekhar?
o: Raman won in 1930 for the Raman Effect, whereas Chandrasekhar won in 1983 for stellar structure and evolution.
Raman won in 1983 for stellar evolution, whereas Chandrasekhar won in 1930 for light scattering.
Both won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on ribosomes.
Both were the first Indian scientist Nobel laureates.
accepted.x: Raman received the 1930 Physics Nobel for light scattering, while Chandrasekhar received the 1983 Physics Nobel for stellar structure and evolution.
accepted.tq: Separate two frequently confused Indian Physics laureates by year and contribution.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the disciplines covered by the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
accepted.x: The seven disciplines include biology, chemistry, earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary sciences, engineering, mathematics, medicine and physics. Political science is not included.

accepted.sec: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize - body, field, age limit, disciplines, recent awardees  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the recent form of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar recognition:
1. It has been folded into the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar.
2. It is known as the Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar award.
3. It is intended for young scientists up to 45 years of age.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The former recognition now appears within the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar framework as VY-SSB for scientists up to 45 years.
accepted.tq: Test a current institutional change through three linked statements.
accepted.sec: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize - body, field, age limit, disciplines, recent awardees  [APPSC]

accepted.x: Madhav Gadgil founded the Centre for Ecological Sciences at the Indian Institute of Science in 1983.

accepted.s: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in

accepted.s: Which of the following represents the original five Nobel Prize categories?
o: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace
Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Agriculture and Economics
Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, Economics and Peace
Physics, Mathematics, Economics, Literature and Peace
accepted.x: The original five categories were Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace. Economics was added later.
accepted.tq: Identify the original list and eliminate the later-added category.
accepted.sec: Nobel Prize - origin, first award year, categories  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Economics prize associated with the Nobel Prize:
1. It was added in 1968.
2. It was first awarded in 1969.
3. Its official name refers to the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel.
4. It was one of the original five prizes specified in Alfred Nobel's will.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Economics was not one of the original five prizes in Nobel's will.
accepted.tq: Use the original-versus-later-added category trap.
accepted.sec: Nobel Prize - origin, first award year, categories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement about Nobel laureate status is correct?
o: It can be revoked by the Nobel Committee after the award ceremony.
It automatically passes to the laureate's institution after death.
It may be transferred permanently to another person along with the medal.
It cannot be transferred, shared or revoked; only the physical medal can change hands.
accepted.x: Nobel laureate status cannot be transferred, shared or revoked. Only the physical medal can change hands.
accepted.tq: Apply the distinction between an honour and the physical award object.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following awards in chronological order of the Indian-origin recipient mentioned:
A. Abel Prize — S.R. Srinivasa Varadhan
B. Fields Medal — Manjul Bhargava
C. International Prize in Statistics — C.R. Rao
D. Turing Award — Raj Reddy
accepted.x: The years are Raj Reddy—1994, S.R. Srinivasa Varadhan—2007, Manjul Bhargava—2014 and C.R. Rao—2023; hence D, A, B, C. Wait, among the options this sequence is option a, not b.
